open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M01 — ObjectConnection
open_points.text: The owner creates and confirms it; the deliverer only reads it.
open_points.question: Who mints the ObjectConnection entity: the owner when creating the connection record, or the Registry when issuing the project_id, as the Identity evidence says?
options: The owner mints the ObjectConnection; the Registry mints only its project_id.
The Registry mints the ObjectConnection when it issues project_id.
The deliverer mints the ObjectConnection from an owner request and an existing Registry project_id.
open_points.default_guess: The owner creates the record, while the Registry mints only the project_id used as its identity.

witness.initial: The Registry has issued project_id P, but no connection record exists.
events: The owner submits folders for P and confirms the assignment.
The deliverer later reads the connection.
outcomes: The owner-created record is the new ObjectConnection entity; the Registry supplied only its key.
The ObjectConnection is treated as an already-minted Registry entity that the owner merely configures.
witness.observer: The owner, Registry adapter and persistence implementation see different creation authority and audit history.

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M01 — ObjectConnection
open_points.text: The same object stays connected while its folders or its confirmation change.
open_points.question: After confirmation, may folders or assignment_confirmed change, may confirmation return to unconfirmed, and does changing a folder require a new confirmation before delivery resumes?
options: A confirmed connection is mutable and stays confirmed after folder changes.
A folder change makes the connection unconfirmed until the owner reconfirms it.
Confirmation is one-way and confirmed connections cannot be edited; replacement requires another action or entity.
open_points.default_guess: A folder change preserves the entity but makes it unconfirmed until the owner reconfirms it.

witness.initial: Project P has a confirmed connection to photo folder A.
events: The owner changes its photo folder to B.
The calling flow asks to scan P before any further confirmation.
outcomes: The deliverer scans B because the connection remains confirmed.
The deliverer refuses the scan because the folder change returned the connection to unconfirmed.
witness.observer: The owner and calling flow see either deliverable photos or an unconfirmed-connection refusal.

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M02 — SourcePhotoObservation
open_points.question: What model fact makes an observation `duplicate`, and duplicate relative to which scope: another file in the same scan, any source content in the project, an existing placement, or something else?
options: It is another pathname in the same project with the same source content.
It is content for which a placement already exists.
It is a duplicate only within the current scan, with canonical-file selection decided later.
open_points.default_guess: It is an additional pathname in the same project whose content has the same source_id as another observed pathname.

witness.initial: A confirmed project's photo folder contains a.jpg and b.jpg with identical bytes, and no placement exists.
events: The calling flow scans the project.
outcomes: One observation is ready and the other is duplicate.
Both observations are ready because duplicate means an already placed source.
witness.observer: The calling flow sees a different set of photos available for placement.

open_points.subject: context
open_points.text: See what can be delivered for a project | each file with a status: ready, placed, published, settling, duplicate or rejected with a reason
open_points.question: Does “each file” include Syncthing temporary files and the phone's trash as observations, or does P-04's statement that they are ignored mean they produce no SourcePhotoObservation at all?
options: Ignored files are absent from scan results.
Ignored files appear as rejected observations with a reason.
Ignored files appear with another listed status.
open_points.default_guess: Ignored files are absent from scan results.

witness.initial: A confirmed photo folder contains one normal image and one Syncthing temporary file.
events: The calling flow asks what can be delivered.
outcomes: The response contains observations for both files because the action reports each file.
The response contains only the normal image because temporary files are ignored under P-04.
witness.observer: The calling flow sees a different number of observations.

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M02 — SourcePhotoObservation
open_points.text: its `source_id` when the content was read
open_points.question: For which statuses must source_id exist, and may settling, rejected or ignored content have no source_id?
options: source_id is present only after content has been read; settling and some rejected observations omit it.
Every returned observation has a source_id, including settling and rejected files.
An observation without source_id is not returned at all.
open_points.default_guess: source_id is optional and absent until content is safely read; settling observations can therefore lack it.

witness.initial: A newly changing file is present in a confirmed photo folder.
events: The deliverer scans it before it has remained unchanged for two minutes.
The calling flow reads the settling observation.
outcomes: The settling observation has no source_id because its content was not read.
The deliverer reads and hashes the changing content and returns a settling observation with source_id.
witness.observer: The calling flow and later placement request see whether the observation identifies content.

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M03 — PreparedPhoto
open_points.text: with the moment the photo was taken as UTC without an offset, and how that moment was obtained, `exif` or `file_modified`
open_points.question: Is date provenance part of PreparedPhoto value identity, despite the Identity evidence saying equal bytes and equal moments are substitutable without mentioning provenance?
options: Provenance is part of the value, so equal pixels and moments with different provenance are different PreparedPhoto values.
Only prepared bytes and moment define the value; provenance is placement metadata outside PreparedPhoto identity.
Provenance is carried but deliberately ignored by value equality.
open_points.default_guess: Provenance is part of PreparedPhoto because the model explicitly carries it and M04 persists it.

witness.initial: Two source files prepare to identical upright pixels and the same UTC moment; one moment came from EXIF and the other from file modification time.
events: A caller or persistence layer compares the PreparedPhoto values.
outcomes: The values differ because exif and file_modified are different model facts.
The values are equal because their bytes and moments are equal.
witness.observer: The placement and persistence implementations see different value equality and metadata.

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M05 — PhotoPublication
open_points.text: The deliverer builds it once within M04.
open_points.question: From what facts does the deliverer mint the PhotoPublication, especially intake_id: is intake_id derived from the placement identity, copied from a caller, or newly generated and then persisted?
options: The deliverer deterministically derives intake_id from project_id and source_id.
The deliverer generates a fresh intake_id when M04 is first created and persists it for replay.
The calling flow supplies intake_id and the deliverer copies it.
open_points.default_guess: The deliverer generates intake_id once while creating M04 and persists the complete body for exact replay.

witness.initial: No placement exists for source S in project P.
events: The owner requests placement of S.
The same placement is requested again.
outcomes: Both calls return a publication body whose intake_id is deterministically derived from P and S.
The first call generates and stores an opaque intake_id, and the replay returns that stored value.
witness.observer: The calling flow and Portal observe different publication identifiers.

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M07 — PublicationMark
open_points.text: The calling flow creates it right after `photo.publish` answers.
open_points.question: Who mints PublicationMark and marked_at: the calling flow, as this passage says, or the deliverer, as the Identity evidence says; does the caller submit a complete mark or only request that the deliverer create one from project_id, source_id and photo_id?
options: The calling flow mints and submits the complete PublicationMark, including marked_at.
The deliverer mints the mark and marked_at after the calling flow submits project_id, source_id and photo_id.
The calling flow mints the logical mark while the deliverer independently assigns marked_at.
open_points.default_guess: The calling flow requests recording with the three identifiers, and the deliverer mints the PublicationMark and marked_at.

witness.initial: Placement S exists and the Portal has just returned photo_id Q.
events: The calling flow invokes the record-publication action.
outcomes: The caller-created mark and caller-chosen marked_at are persisted.
The deliverer creates the mark and assigns marked_at at receipt.
witness.observer: The calling flow, deliverer and audit reader see different creation authority and timestamps.

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M07 — PublicationMark
open_points.text: The same `photo_id` again returns the first mark; another `photo_id` is refused.
open_points.question: Is this idempotency rule scoped only to one placement, and may the same Portal photo_id be marked for two different placements or projects?
options: photo_id is globally unique across all PublicationMarks and a second placement using it is refused.
photo_id is unique only within a project.
Only placement identity is unique; the same photo_id may appear on marks for different placements.
open_points.default_guess: A Portal photo_id may belong to only one PublicationMark globally, so reuse for another placement is refused.

witness.initial: Placements A and B exist and neither is marked.
events: The calling flow records Portal photo_id Q for A.
The calling flow then records the same Q for B.
outcomes: The second action is refused because one Portal photo cannot represent two placements.
A second mark is created because the stated conflict rule checks only whether B already has another photo_id.
witness.observer: The calling flow, scan results and owner see whether two source photos claim the same Portal photo.

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:preamble
open_points.text:
Field types and the complete field lists belong to the
State 6 model closure.
open_points.question: The State 1 model definitions must state every field with its type instead of deferring the field lists and types to State 6.
